test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT true about an object in non-uniform motion?

options.text: The change in velocity is zero over time interval
It moves unequal distances in unequal time intervals
It has different speeds at different points

solution:
The correct answer is __**The change in velocity is zero over time interval**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-uniform motion** is defined as the motion of an object in which the object travels with **varied speed** and does not cover the same distance in equal time intervals.
 
• In **non-uniform motion**, the **velocity** of the object does not remain constant. Since velocity is a **vector quantity**, it changes if either the **speed** (magnitude) or the **direction** of motion changes.
 
• The statement "The change in velocity is zero over time interval" implies that the **initial velocity** and **final velocity** are identical, which means the **acceleration** is zero. This is a characteristic of **Uniform Motion**, not non-uniform motion. ***Hence, statement 1 is NOT true.***
 
• An object in non-uniform motion covers **unequal distances** in **equal intervals of time**. By extension, the relationship between distance and time is not linear, meaning it can move unequal distances in unequal time intervals depending on the **rate of acceleration**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct in the context of non-uniformity.***
 
• Because the rate of motion is constantly fluctuating, the object will possess **different speeds** at different points or instances along its path. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The core definition of non-uniform motion is that the **velocity changes with time**. This change indicates the presence of **acceleration** (positive or negative). ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration**: In **non-uniform motion**, the **acceleration** of the body is **non-zero**. Acceleration is the measure of the **rate of change of velocity** with respect to **time**. If the velocity increases, it is called acceleration; if it decreases, it is called **retardation** or **deceleration**.
 
• **Types of Non-Uniform Motion**:
 
 
• **Uniformly Accelerated Motion**: The velocity changes by **equal amounts** in equal intervals of time (e.g., a ball rolling down an inclined plane).
 
• **Non-uniformly Accelerated Motion**: The velocity changes by **unequal amounts** in equal intervals of time (e.g., a car moving in heavy city traffic).
 
 
 
• **Average Speed**: For an object in non-uniform motion, the **average speed** is calculated by dividing the **total distance** traveled by the **total time taken**. Unlike uniform motion, the **instantaneous speed** at any given point is usually different from the average speed.
 
• **Examples**: Common real-world examples include a **train** pulling out of a station, a **person jogging** in a crowded park, or a **pendulum** swinging back and forth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Graphical Representation**:

 
 
• In a **Distance-Time Graph**, non-uniform motion is represented by a **curved line** (parabola or zig-zag), indicating that the **slope** (speed) is changing.
 
• In a **Velocity-Time Graph**, non-uniform motion is represented by any line that is **not horizontal**. A horizontal line would indicate constant velocity (uniform motion).
 
 
 
• **Uniform Motion vs. Non-Uniform Motion**:
 
 
• **Uniform Motion**: Covers equal distance in equal time; **zero acceleration**; **constant velocity**.
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion**: Covers unequal distance in equal time; **variable acceleration**; **changing velocity**.
 
 
 
• **Directional Change**: It is important to note that even if an object moves at a **constant speed** in a circle (**Uniform Circular Motion**), it is considered **non-uniform motion** because its **direction** is constantly changing, resulting in a change in **velocity**.
